title: Chinese Money Markets Signal Credit Growth is Slowing Again
content: A rare dislocation in China’s money markets is pointing to a buildup of liquidity, which analysts say is a sign of slowing credit growth.

title: Mercer Bonds Sink as Pulp Firm Seeks to Strip Lender Protections
content: Mercer International Inc.’s bonds slumped after it sought to ditch rules requiring equal treatment for all creditors — a move that would give the struggling pulp producer the power to pick and choose which lenders to favor in a restructuring.

title: World Bank Pres. on Hormuz Disruptions, De-dollarization
content: World Bank President Ajay Banga discusses the economic fallout from ongoing disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, inflation risks in emerging markets, crisis-response capacity and the broader outlook for growth. Banga also downplays concerns that geopolitical tensions could meaningfully weaken the dollar’s role in global lending. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg's Balance of Power. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Japan FSA Watching Private Credit Risks, Sees Limited Exposure
content: Japanese financial firms have “limited” exposure to private credit in the US even after expanding such investments in recent years, the nation’s financial regulator told the ruling party, as concerns mount over risks in the sector.

title: Barclays Sounds Out Investors for a Shutterfly Refinancing Deal
content: Barclays PLC is sounding out potential investors to help Shutterfly push out its looming debt pile, after talks with private credit lenders lost momentum.

title: 5 Interesting Startup Deals You May Have Missed: A Credit Card Backed By Mineral Rights, Flying Ferries, And A Foundation AI Model For Plants
content: In a quarter when nearly two-thirds of global venture capital went to just four companies, it’s easy to lose track of the many other companies getting funding to tackle interesting problems. We spotted five companies in just the past month working on issues from cleaner ferries and trains to foundational AI for the crop industry.

title: Exclusive: Miravoice, Builder Of An AI ‘Interviewer’ To Conduct Phone Surveys, Raises $6.3M
content: Miravoice, a startup using AI voice agents to conduct long-form phone surveys, has raised $6.3 million in a seed funding round, the company tells Crunchbase News exclusively.

title: The Largest Recent Seed Rounds Are All For AI Companies
content: A majority of top seed funding recipients in the past six months operate at the intersection of AI and the physical world. Using Crunchbase data, we take a look at some of the sector's biggest seed rounds in recent months.

title: Seed Funding Hasn’t Stalled, But It’s Skewing Larger And Is More Competitive Than Ever, Crunchbase Data Shows
content: Among U.S. seed funding deals, it’s only the upper bands of larger and outlier seed rounds — those $10 million and above — that grew in 2025, Crunchbase data shows.
